pending_interview.category: Martech/AI-product — personalization architecture, attribution modeling, GenAI content pipelines, measurement under privacy constraints
pending_interview.question: You're advising a direct-to-consumer brand that has been using a third-party identity graph to power personalized email and paid media campaigns. New privacy regulations have sharply limited cross-site tracking, and their third-party data provider has told them their match rates (the percentage of users the provider can actually identify and connect to behavioral data) are down 40% year-over-year. The brand still wants to run personalized campaigns and measure whether those campaigns actually caused purchases — not just correlated with them. Walk me through how you would redesign their personalization and attribution architecture for a privacy-constrained environment. What data assets would you prioritize building, what measurement approaches would you rely on, and what are the key tradeoffs you'd flag for their marketing leadership?
